module_title: Finding the Right Machine for Your Market

lessons.title: Assessing Local Demand: What Do Farmers, Builders, and Processors Need?
lessons.body: Before you buy any machine, you must know who will pay to use it. Start by walking through your local area and talking to at least 20 potential customers. For farmers, ask what tasks take the most time and labour. In many African communities, maize shelling, cassava grinding, and groundnut oil pressing are top needs. A farmer with 2 hectares of maize may spend 10 days shelling by hand; a small maize sheller can do that in 2 hours. That saves 9 days of labour, which is worth about 50,000 to 100,000 shillings depending on local wages. For builders, demand often centres on block-making, concrete mixing, and cutting iron sheets. A manual block-making machine can produce 500 blocks per day, while a motorised one can do 1,500. Check how many building projects are within 20 km of your location. For processors, look at what raw materials are abundant. If there is a lot of cassava, a cassava grater and press are needed. If there are many oilseeds, an oil expeller is profitable. Visit local markets and ask traders what products they buy from outside the area. That tells you what processing is missing. Also check existing machines: if three people already own a maize mill, the market may be saturated. A simple demand survey tool is a notebook and pen. Record names, phone numbers, and specific needs. After 20 interviews, you will see a pattern. Choose the machine that solves the most common, most painful problem. That is your best bet for steady income.

lessons.title: The 10 Most Profitable Small Machines in Africa
lessons.body: Based on real earnings across Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, and Tanzania, these 10 small Chinese machines consistently make money. 1) Maize sheller: costs $200-$500, shells 1-2 tonnes per hour. Charge $5 per 50kg bag; 20 bags a day = $100. 2) Cassava grater: $300-$600, grates 500kg per hour. Custom grating earns $0.05 per kg; 2 tonnes daily = $100. 3) Groundnut oil expeller: $500-$1,200, presses 50kg per hour. Oil sells for $2-$3 per litre; 20 litres per day = $40-$60 profit. 4) Rice mill: $800-$2,000, mills 500kg per hour. Milling fee $0.03 per kg; 2 tonnes = $60. 5) Block-making machine: manual $400, motorised $1,500. Manual makes 500 blocks per day; each block sells for $0.30 = $150. 6) Concrete mixer: $300-$800, mixes 200 litres per batch. Rent for $20 per day. 7) Welding machine: $150-$400, charges $5-$10 per job. 8) Water pump: $200-$500, irrigates 1 acre per day. Rent for $10-$15 daily. 9) Poultry feed pellet machine: $400-$900, makes 100kg per hour. Sell pellets at $0.50 per kg = $50 per hour. 10) Cassava press: $300-$700, presses 200kg per hour. Charge $0.10 per kg = $20 per hour. These numbers assume you find customers. Always start with the machine that matches your local raw materials and skills. For example, if you are near a lake, a water pump for irrigation is gold. If you are in a maize belt, a sheller is safer. The key is not the machine alone but the demand you can serve.

lessons.title: Matching Machine Capacity to Your Market Size
lessons.body: Buying a machine that is too big wastes money; too small loses customers. First, estimate your daily demand. Count how many farmers, builders, or processors need your service within a 10 km radius. For example, if 50 farmers each have 1 hectare of maize, that is 50 hectares. A hectare yields about 2 tonnes of maize. Total 100 tonnes. Shelling season lasts 3 weeks (21 days). So you need to shell 100,000 kg / 21 days = 4,762 kg per day. A small sheller does 1,000 kg per hour. You need 5 hours of work per day. That is manageable. If you buy a machine that does 5,000 kg per hour, you will only work 1 hour per day and waste fuel and capital. Second, check your power source. Chinese machines often come with diesel or electric motors. A 5 HP diesel engine uses about 1 litre per hour. If you run 5 hours, that is 5 litres = $5. Electric motors are cheaper per hour but need reliable power. Third, consider transport. If your customers are far, you may need to move the machine. A small, portable machine (under 100 kg) is better than a heavy one. Fourth, think about growth. If you expect demand to double in 2 years, buy a machine that can be upgraded or run at higher speed. But do not overbuy. A good rule: buy a machine that can handle 120% of your current peak daily demand. That gives room to grow without sitting idle. Always ask the seller for the machine's capacity in kg per hour or blocks per day. If they cannot tell you, walk away. Real numbers matter.

lessons.title: New vs. Refurbished: Pros and Cons
lessons.body: New Chinese machines come with a warranty, usually 6 to 12 months. They are cleaner, more reliable, and often have better fuel efficiency. But they cost 30% to 50% more than refurbished ones. For example, a new maize sheller might cost $500, while a refurbished one is $300. Refurbished machines are used machines that have been repaired and repainted. They can work well if the repair was done properly. However, you must inspect them carefully. Check for cracks in the frame, worn bearings, and rust in the engine. Ask for a demonstration with actual maize or cassava. Listen for unusual noises. A good refurbished machine can last 2-3 years, while a new one can last 5-7 years. If you have limited capital and a reliable mechanic nearby, refurbished can be a good start. But if you need the machine for daily income and cannot afford downtime, buy new. Also consider spare parts: new machines often use standard parts that are easy to find. Refurbished machines may have modified parts that are hard to replace. One smart strategy: buy a new machine for your main income earner, and a refurbished one for backup or for less critical tasks. Another factor is resale value. New machines hold value better. If you plan to upgrade in 2 years, new is better. If you plan to use it until it dies, refurbished is fine. Always get a receipt and a written guarantee, even for refurbished. Test the machine under load for at least 30 minutes before paying. Never buy without seeing it run.

lessons.title: The Importance of Spare Parts Availability
lessons.body: A machine without spare parts is a pile of metal. Before you buy any Chinese machine, find out where you can buy parts. Ask the seller: Where is your nearest parts dealer? How long does it take to order a replacement? What are the most common parts that break? For maize shellers, the rubber rollers and sieves wear out. For oil expellers, the pressing screws and rings wear. For block-making machines, the moulds and bearings wear. If you cannot find these parts locally, you may wait weeks for a shipment from China. That means lost income. A simple rule: only buy a machine if you can find at least two suppliers of its spare parts within 100 km. If not, consider a different brand or model. Also, learn to do basic maintenance yourself. Change oil every 100 hours of use. Grease bearings every 50 hours. Keep the machine clean. A well-maintained machine breaks less often. But even with care, parts wear out. So budget 10% of the machine's cost per year for spare parts. For a $500 machine, set aside $50 per year. That is $4 per month. When a part breaks, you can fix it immediately. Another tip: buy a machine that uses common parts. For example, many Chinese diesel engines use standard oil filters that are also used in motorcycles. That makes them easy to find. Avoid machines with unique, proprietary parts. Ask other owners in your area what they use and where they buy parts. Their experience is your best guide.

lessons.title: When a Small Machine Beats a Large One
lessons.body: Bigger is not always better. In many African markets, a small machine outperforms a large one. Here is why. First, small machines cost less to buy and maintain. A small maize sheller at $300 can be paid off in 2 months. A large one at $3,000 might take 2 years. Second, small machines are easier to move. If your customers are scattered, you can carry a 50 kg machine on a motorcycle. A 500 kg machine needs a truck. Third, small machines use less fuel. A 3 HP engine uses 0.5 litres per hour; a 10 HP engine uses 2 litres per hour. If you only have 2 hours of work, the small machine is cheaper. Fourth, small machines are less risky. If demand drops, you can sell it easily or use it for other tasks. A large machine may sit idle. Fifth, small machines are easier to repair. You can learn to fix them yourself. Large machines need specialised mechanics. When does a large machine win? When you have a guaranteed, high-volume contract. For example, if a large farm hires you to shell 50 tonnes of maize in one week, a large machine is better. But most small businesses start with small machines and upgrade later. A good strategy: start with a small machine, serve your local market, save profits, then buy a second small machine or a larger one when demand is proven. Do not buy a large machine hoping to find customers. Buy a small machine that you know you can keep busy. That is the safest path to profit.

quiz.q: What is the first step before buying any machine?
quiz.explanation: You must know who will pay for the machine's service before investing.

quiz.q: How many potential customers should you interview for a basic demand survey?
quiz.explanation: Interviewing at least 20 people helps you see a clear pattern of needs.

quiz.q: Which machine is listed as profitable for maize farmers?
quiz.explanation: A maize sheller saves labour and can earn $100 per day by shelling 20 bags.

quiz.q: What is a typical cost range for a small maize sheller?
quiz.explanation: Small Chinese maize shellers typically cost between $200 and $500.

quiz.q: Which machine is best if you are near a lake and need irrigation?
quiz.explanation: Water pumps are ideal for irrigation and can be rented out daily.

quiz.q: What does a block-making machine produce?
quiz.explanation: Block-making machines produce concrete blocks for building.

quiz.q: How many blocks per day can a manual block-making machine produce?
quiz.explanation: A manual block-making machine can produce about 500 blocks per day.

quiz.q: What is the first step to match machine capacity to your market?
quiz.explanation: You must estimate how much work you will have each day before choosing capacity.

quiz.q: If 50 farmers each have 1 hectare of maize, how many tonnes of maize need shelling?
quiz.explanation: 50 hectares at 2 tonnes per hectare equals 100 tonnes.

quiz.q: What is a good rule for machine capacity?
quiz.explanation: Buying 120% of current peak demand allows room to grow without idle capacity.

quiz.q: Why is a small, portable machine often better?
options: A) It is cheaper to buy and move
quiz.explanation: Small machines cost less, are easier to transport, and use less fuel.

quiz.q: What should you check first when buying a refurbished machine?
options: C) For cracks, worn bearings, and rust
quiz.explanation: Inspect for structural damage and worn parts before buying.

quiz.q: How much more do new machines typically cost compared to refurbished?
quiz.explanation: New Chinese machines usually cost 30% to 50% more than refurbished ones.

quiz.q: What is a smart strategy when buying machines?
options: C) Buy new for main income, refurbished for backup
quiz.explanation: This balances reliability for critical tasks with cost savings for less critical ones.

quiz.q: Why is a written guarantee important even for refurbished machines?
options: B) It protects you if the machine fails
C) It is required by law
quiz.explanation: A guarantee gives you recourse if the machine breaks soon after purchase.

quiz.q: What should you do before paying for any machine?
options: A) Test it under load for 30 minutes
quiz.explanation: Running the machine under load reveals any hidden problems.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to find out about spare parts?
options: B) Where to buy them locally
quiz.explanation: Local availability of spare parts prevents long downtime.

quiz.q: How many spare parts suppliers should be within 100 km?
quiz.explanation: Having at least two suppliers gives you options and reduces risk.

quiz.q: How often should you change oil in a small machine?
quiz.explanation: Changing oil every 100 hours of use keeps the engine healthy.

quiz.q: What percentage of machine cost should you budget yearly for spare parts?
quiz.explanation: Budgeting 10% of the machine's cost per year covers typical part replacements.

quiz.q: Why are common parts better than proprietary parts?
options: B) They are easier to find
quiz.explanation: Common parts are widely available, reducing downtime.

quiz.q: What is a sign that a machine may be a bad buy?
options: A) It uses standard oil filters
B) It has unique, hard-to-find parts
C) It comes with a warranty
quiz.explanation: Unique parts can be difficult and slow to replace.

quiz.q: When does a small machine beat a large one?
options: A) When you have a huge contract
B) When demand is low or scattered
D) When you have no customers
quiz.explanation: Small machines are more efficient for low, scattered demand.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of small machines regarding risk?
options: A) They are easier to sell if demand drops
quiz.explanation: Small machines have better resale value and can be repurposed.

quiz.q: How much fuel does a 3 HP engine use per hour?
quiz.explanation: A 3 HP engine typically uses about 0.5 litres per hour.

quiz.q: What is a safe strategy for starting a machine business?
options: A) Buy a large machine first
B) Start with a small machine and upgrade later
C) Buy three machines at once
D) Borrow heavily for a large machine
quiz.explanation: Starting small lets you prove demand and save profits before expanding.

quiz.q: Why might a large machine sit idle?
options: B) Demand is not high enough
C) It uses too little fuel
D) It is too easy to repair
quiz.explanation: Without enough work, a large machine becomes an expensive idle asset.

quiz.q: What should you do if a seller cannot tell you the machine's capacity?
quiz.explanation: A seller who does not know capacity may be hiding poor performance.

quiz.q: Which of these is a real method to assess demand?
quiz.explanation: Direct interviews give you specific, local data on needs.

quiz.q: What is the main risk of buying a refurbished machine without testing?
options: B) It may have hidden defects
C) It will be too new
D) It will use too little fuel
quiz.explanation: Hidden defects can cause immediate breakdowns and lost income.
